subject: Error using Wald in DIF testing

messages.author: 885539f3f5ae8fd5
messages.subject: Error using Wald in DIF testing
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm trying to decide whether I should be using a Wald test or a log-likelihood test when trying to detect DIF between two groups. When I try using the Wald = TRUE argument though, I get the following error:

itemtypes <- c("2PL", "2PL", "2PL", "graded", "2PL", "2PL", "2PL", "2PL")
mod <- multipleGroup(data[ ,c("2_1","2_2","2_3","2_4","2_5","2_6","2_7","2_8")], model = 1, itemtype = itemtypes, guess = 0, upper = 1, group = as.character(data$gender))
out <- DIF(mod, c("a1", "d"), plotdif = TRUE, Wald = TRUE, p.adjust = "fdr")
> Error: Information matrix was not calculated

(In addition to the hyper-parameters warning, which to be honest I don't understand at all.)

Do you know why I might be getting the information matrix error? I don't think it's an an insufficient data problem, as I have over 2,000 students in my data set. Also, there are no errors fitting the IRT model itself, and there's no problem when I leave Wald = FALSE.

Thanks,
Jon

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Error using Wald in DIF testing
parts:
Hi Jon,

You need to pass SE=TRUE to your multipleGroup() call in order to obtain the information matrix/ACOV. Then you can do wald tests. 

The second warning is about equating the groups. DIF from a likelihood perspective requires equating, meaning selecting anchor items to equate certain parameters and freely estimating the latent trait distributions in the focal group (i.e., mean and variances). There are some examples in the multipleGroup help file which are likely helpful, and David Thissen has a nice intro to the topic which comes with his IRT-LRDIF sofware here: http://www.unc.edu/~dthissen/dl.html. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Error using Wald in DIF testing
parts:
They will be on the same scale so long as 1) anchor items are modelled, and 2) the latent trait hyper-parameters in the focal group(s) are freely estimated. My paper on DTF in EPM discusses this technique as well if you are less familiar with the setup. Cheers.

Phil
